newsitem.title: GERMANY: German call money steady, banks eye reserve target.
newsitem.headline: German call money steady, banks eye reserve target.

text.p: German call rates were largely steady on Monday and appeared unlikely to fall in the short-term as banks realised they might still need to hold more reserves to meet the Bundesbank's monthly reserve target.
Rates traded largely unchanged from Friday's levels at between three percent and 3.05 percent.

Although rates had often touched the three percent repo level in recent weeks, dealers this morning said rates traded near the upper end of the range because their holdings at the central bank were not sufficient to meet the Bundesbank's June preliminary 39.8 billion mark reserve goal, released on Monday.
"The cheap times under three percent are gone," one trader said.

Banks held 39 billion marks with the central bank on Friday, leaving the average for the months so far at 40.1 billion marks. But the actual goal is usually over one billion marks higher, forcing banks to hold quite a bit of reserves in the next five days before exiry.
Only around 100 million marks was borrowed from the Lombard lending facility.
The Frankfurt Interbank Overnight Average stood at 3.05467 percent on Monday compared with 3.04400 percent.
